PullRequest.Title: sessions: add Close Others to the chat tab context menu
PullRequest.Body:
Right-clicking a chat tab in the Agents window now offers **Close Others**. It closes the other tabs in the strip and keeps the one you clicked. Today you can close tabs one at a time or all at once with **Close All Chats**, but there is no way to keep just one.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebd05d17-9585-439d-a2e2-3c6471ed78a4

The strip starts with five tabs. Right-click the last one, choose **Close Others**, and the main chat and the tab you clicked are left.

## What changed

- Added **Close Others** to the chat tab context menu, next to **Close**. It only shows when another tab can be closed.
- The main chat always stays, because no tab can close it. On the main chat's own tab, **Close Others** closes every other tab.
- If the active tab closes, the tab you clicked becomes active. If the main chat was active, it stays active.
- Closed chats stay in the session, so they are still in the sidebar and in the chats dropdown in the session header.
- Like **Close All Chats**, the batch is not offered to **Reopen Closed Chat**, because that would only bring back the last chat. Both actions now share one helper, and both delete untitled drafts, since there is nothing to reopen.
- The new command is `sessions.chatCompositeBar.closeOtherChats`. It is not in the Command Palette because it needs the tab it keeps.
- Added a line about **Close Others** to the chat accessibility help, shown when chat tabs are in multiple mode, because the command is only in the tab context menu.
- Updated the two tab menu expectations in the existing tests, and added a three-tab menu test and tests for the action, including which chat ends up selected for the main chat, a side chat, and a split group.

## Before and after

The menu, with the new item highlighted:

Before, with five tabs:

![The chat tab strip with five tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8058e0c-6d8f-4d8a-a979-449e61c944f9)

After, with the main chat and the tab that was clicked:

![The chat tab strip with two tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32d5498c-bd94-4853-901c-530667d966d5)

## Try it

Set `sessions.showChatTabs` to `multiple`, open a session with a few chats, right-click a tab, and choose **Close Others**.

## About the video

In the video, the agent is a scripted demo agent, so the replies are canned. The tab strip and the context menu are the real UI from this branch.

## Open question

**Should Close Others show on the main chat's tab?** It does now, and it closes every other tab, which is the same as Close All Chats. I can hide it there if that is redundant.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The individual publication, reconciliation autorun, full tab rebuild, and per-reconcile persistence paths are directly traced. Only the exact latency depends on realistic tab and group counts.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, tab actions/listeners/observables, reconciliation CPU, temporary arrays/sets/JSON, and workspace storage operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Closing T chats triggers T reconciliations and rebuilds T-1 through zero remaining tabs, producing O(T^2) widget construction; a split layout can also be serialized and stored T times.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Synchronous UI latency, CPU and GC pressure, and repeated storage I/O
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Close Others did not exist, so no single context-menu action synchronously published all other tab closures one at a time. Close All already used an equivalent loop, and this refactor preserves that pre-existing cost while newly applying it to Close Others.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added shared helper loops over every target chat and awaits an individual close or delete, publishing a distinct visibility update for each committed chat.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `for (const chat of chats)` at line 1247 makes both batch gestures execute as a sequence of individual state changes; the new Close Others action calls this helper with all other strip chats.
Findings.Title: Publish the batch close only once
Findings.Impact: Closing the other tabs in a large strip can block the UI while the remaining tab strip and group layout are reconstructed repeatedly instead of once.
Findings.Evidence: Every committed iteration reaches SessionsService.closeChat and SessionSlotState.closeChat, which clones and publishes `_closedChatUris` in its own transaction. That publication reruns ChatGroupsView reconciliation and, for the affected group, ChatCompositeBar `_rebuildTabs`, which clears and recreates every remaining tab widget and listener. Split layouts also call `_persistLayout`, parsing, serializing, and storing layout state after each publication.
Findings.Recommendation: Provide a batch visibility-close operation that computes and publishes the final closed/shown sets and persisted state once in one transaction, causing one reconciliation and tab rebuild; keep required ordering for draft deletion and external-host closure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a chat tab context menu and decide whether Close Others is available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The context-menu event synchronously builds its action list; the added predicate filters the current strip chats once before the menu can appear.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in the clicked tab's strip; one linear scan with no retained result.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous on the UI thread; no queue, limiter, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads current observable chat arrays directly so the menu is always current; no cache, miss path, or coalescing is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added closure and filter are directly in the context-menu getActions path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical strips are small and the scan is simple; very large strips increase only linearly.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. One linear identity-filter pass per explicitly opened menu is proportionate and does not cross an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Close Others on committed chats in one or more chat groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: If the currently shown chat will close, one awaited openChat selection completes first. The command then awaits every individual close; each visibility publication, group reconciliation, tab rebuild, and split-layout persistence occurs before command completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/parse and JSON-stringify/store workspace chat-group layout state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one storage read and write per committed chat closed when a multi-group layout remains, so O(T) boundary operations; each serialization covers the full saved-layout map.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Close Others command put T individual layout publications into one gesture. Individual manual closes persisted separately between gestures; Close All has the same pre-existing implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously from each reconciliation on the command path and adds directly to Close Others latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T effective closable chats in the clicked strip after excluding the kept and main chats. There is no deduplication beyond those resource filters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The helper is strictly serialized by an await inside the loop. Observable/UI effects publish independently per item rather than under one outer transaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The displayed session and tab catalog are warm/current. Identity checks read current observables. There is no batching or coalescing cache for visibility updates; split-layout persistence rereads and reserializes the stored layout map for each close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the new command reaches the added per-item helper; every local close publishes a new set, the group autorun reconciles it, and ChatCompositeBar clears and recreates all remaining tab widgets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact delay depends on tab count, number of groups, widget complexity, and stored-layout size. The repeated full rebuild is certain; common five-tab examples may be modest while large overflowing strips and split layouts amplify it.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression submitted: T individual publications cause O(T^2) tab-widget reconstruction and repeated layout persistence instead of one final batch update.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Close Others when other tabs include untitled drafts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each draft deletion is awaited in sequence before the action resolves; provider disposal and resulting catalog/UI updates are on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose one agent-host chat through connection.disposeChat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC/provider operation per untitled draft, D operations, serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Close Others did not previously put all draft deletions on one action path; Close All and separate manual deletion already used individual provider operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All D operations must finish sequentially before Close Others resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: D untitled drafts among the T effective closable chats. No grouping or deduplication occurs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one provider deletion is in flight because the loop serially awaits each item; this avoids a burst but makes latency additive.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The unsent check consults the current session/chat model. Provider deletion has no result cache, negative cache, or coalescing because every draft is a distinct resource.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the D serialized boundary calls, lower for a realistically large D.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not establish that users commonly accumulate many simultaneous untitled drafts, and each distinct draft genuinely requires disposal. Provider round-trip duration is also unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. The fan-out is real but distinct resources require deletion, no bulk provider API was found, and realistic draft cardinality is not established; batching the local visibility updates remains the actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run Close All Chats after the helper refactor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action computes non-main open chats and executes the same sequential close/delete behavior it used before the PR, now through the shared helper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete each untitled draft through the sessions provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged at one operation per untitled draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted inline loop performed the same status check, awaited deleteChat for drafts, and awaited closeChat for committed chats in the same order.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All non-main open chats in the active pane.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized before and after the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged: current pane chats are read directly and each visibility/delete operation retains its prior cache and persistence behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct before/after diff comparison.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful uncertainty: the old and new loops are behaviorally equivalent for this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression and no regression-fix record. The refactor preserves Close All's pre-existing performance characteristics.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: When accessibility help is requested, one localized string is conditionally appended for multiple-tab mode.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work independent of chat or session count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or external lookup beyond normal localization formatting; no repeated collection work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files. One medium repeated-work finding was submitted for Close Others publishing each tab closure separately, which provably causes triangular full-tab reconstruction and repeated split-layout persistence. Context-menu filtering and accessibility help are bounded; draft IPC fan-out is serialized but lacks a realistic high-cardinality trigger or bulk alternative; Close All's refactor preserves its prior behavior.
